title: Introduction to Programming and Computer Science - Full Course
editorNote: Explains what a program actually is — variables, control flow, functions, data — before any syntax, then walks through how the machine executes it. Runs ~2 hours, so a complete beginner can finish it in a week and arrive at a first language course with the right mental model.

title: Algorithms and Data Structures Tutorial - Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Covers arrays, linked lists, hash tables, trees, graphs and the classic algorithms with hand-traced examples and complexity analysis in every section. The implementations are typed out on screen rather than shown as finished code, which makes it usable as a do-it-alongside course.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms in Python - Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Twelve and a half hours of Python implementations of every structure and algorithm in the companion course, ending with interview-style problem walkthroughs. Use it when you want the algorithm practice to double as Python practice.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms Mega Course – Master Technical Interviews in 49 Hours
editorNote: A 49-hour mega course published in late 2025 that goes past the classic curriculum into pattern-based interview preparation. The most current large-scale DSA pack we verified, and the only one that also covers how to structure practice sessions.

title: Computer Science
editorNote: 41 short episodes that build from logic gates to operating systems, networking and the web. The fastest way to fill the gaps that make later courses feel like magic; each episode is about 12 minutes so it fits between practice sessions.

title: Learn Python - Full Course for Beginners [Tutorial]
editorNote: The canonical freeCodeCamp Python course: four and a half hours from installing Python to functions, classes, modules and small projects, with the instructor typing every line. It moves slowly enough for a first language and still reaches object-oriented code.

title: Python for Beginners – Full Course [Programming Tutorial]
editorNote: A newer freeCodeCamp beginner course (2022) with the same scope as the 2018 original but modern idioms — f-strings, virtual environments, modern tooling. Good second voice if the first course's pace or accent did not click.

title: Python Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Two hours, published in 2025, and ruthlessly edited: only the syntax you will use in the first month, with clear diagrams for lists, dictionaries and functions. The best choice when you need to be productive in Python this week and can revisit details later.

title: Python Tutorial for Beginners (with mini-projects)
editorNote: Eight and a half hours built entirely around mini-projects, so every concept arrives with something to build. This is the resource to pair with any syntax course to move from 'I understand the video' to 'I can make something'.

title: Harvard CS50’s Introduction to Programming with Python – Full University Course
editorNote: Harvard's CS50P as a single 16-hour video: nine lectures plus problem sets, with real grading criteria and a formal introduction to testing and exceptions. The strongest structure of any free Python course we verified for learners who want accountability.

title: Intermediate Python Programming Course
editorNote: Picks up exactly where beginner courses stop: comprehensions, generators, decorators, collections, itertools, regex and typing. Six hours of dense material that removes the gap between 'knows Python syntax' and 'can read other people's Python'.

title: Python Tutorial for Beginners 8: Functions
editorNote: Twenty-two minutes on functions, arguments, defaults, *args/**kwargs and scope — the single most common source of beginner confusion, explained with clear terminal demos. Use it as a clarifier the moment the syntax course hand-waves parameters.

title: Python for AI - Full Beginner Course
editorNote: Five hours of Python taught through the lens of AI applications — Pydantic models, API calls, data processing — instead of generic exercises. Published in 2025, it is the most direct bridge from Python basics to the AI roadmap.

title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Full Course for Beginners - Build a Full-Stack Web App
editorNote: Corey Schafer's 2025 FastAPI series cut into one 14-hour course: routing, validation, databases, auth and deployment while building a real application. It is the rare case where the 2026 publish date and the teaching quality line up.

title: FastAPI Course for Beginners
editorNote: One hour to a working API — app object, paths, request bodies, docs UI. Enough to decide whether FastAPI is the right tool before committing to the 14-hour course.

title: Python Django 7 Hour Course
editorNote: A full Django build — models, migrations, templates, admin, auth, Postgres — with the same project carried from empty folder to deployment. The most complete single-video Django walkthrough still standing.

title: Automate with Python – Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Teaches Python through the jobs people actually want automated: renaming files in bulk, pulling data from PDFs and spreadsheets, scheduling scripts. Best first-project resource after the syntax course because the payoff is visible immediately.

title: Python Tutorials
editorNote: 158 topic-sized Python videos — one concept each — from Corey Schafer's long-running series. Not a linear course: treat it as a video encyclopedia to consult when a specific topic (slicing, generators, virtualenvs) needs a second explanation.

title: Python OOP Tutorials - Working with Classes
editorNote: Six videos building one coherent class hierarchy step by step — instances, class variables, inheritance, special methods, decorators. Under 90 minutes total and still the clearest OOP walkthrough on YouTube for Python.

title: Git & GitHub Crash Course for Beginners [2026]
editorNote: An 81-minute 2025 freeCodeCamp/Logiclear course that covers init, commits, branches, merges and your first pull request — everything a beginner needs, with current GitHub UI. The freshest strong Git resource we verified.

title: Git and GitHub - Full Course
editorNote: Four hours that go under the hood — the commit graph, HEAD, rebase vs merge, reflog recovery — with a terminal you can follow. This is the course that stops Git from being magic and makes mistakes recoverable.

title: Learn Git – Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Nearly four hours of slow, methodical Git and GitHub instruction, published 2024, including collaboration workflows and GitHub features. A good alternative when a learner wants one resource that covers both Git and GitHub in depth.

title: The 50 Most Popular Linux & Terminal Commands - Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Five hours structured around the fifty commands that cover daily work — navigation, files, permissions, processes, networking, package management — each demonstrated in a terminal rather than described. The practical entry point for the Linux skill.

title: Learn Linux - The Full Course
editorNote: A 2025 refresher course that treats the shell as a programming environment — scripting, pipes, environment setup — instead of a list of commands. Better once you know the basics and want to automate.

title: Linux Command Line for Beginners
editorNote: One hour of essentials for someone who needs to stop fearing the terminal today — navigation, editing, permissions, ssh. It assumes no prior shell use and avoids detours.

title: Linux Zero to Hero | Free Linux Course
editorNote: Thirteen videos (about nine and a half hours) that teach Linux in the context a DevOps learner meets it: servers, users, networking, services and troubleshooting on real VMs.

title: Linux for Hackers (and everyone) // FREE Course for Beginners
editorNote: NetworkChuck's ten-episode 'Linux for Hackers' series builds a Linux skill set with a security flavour — permissions, users, services, scripting — and each episode ends with a hands-on task in a lab VM.

title: Linux Server Course - System Configuration and Operation
editorNote: Five and a half hours on running a Linux server: systemd services, networking, DNS, web servers, logs and package management. Bridges the gap between 'I can use the shell' and 'I can keep a server alive'.

title: SQL Course for Beginners [Full Course]
editorNote: Three hours of SQL taught against a realistic store database, with joins, grouping and subqueries introduced in the order you meet them in practice. The clearest single-video SQL foundation in the set.

title: Learn SQL Beginner to Advanced in Under 4 Hours
editorNote: Takes SQL from basics to window functions and CTEs with a data-analyst framing — how to answer a business question, not just how to run a query. Published 2024, so the tooling screenshots are current.

title: Relational Database Design – Full Course
editorNote: Six hours on relational design — entities, keys, relationships, normal forms, constraints — taught with diagrams and then implemented. The resource that prevents the schema mistakes most developers make on their first real project.

title: Learn Database Normalization - 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, 4NF, 5NF
editorNote: Twenty-nine minutes that finally make 1NF through 5NF click, using worked transformations of the same table rather than abstract rules. Ideal as a refresher before a design review.

title: PostgreSQL Tutorial for Beginners
editorNote: A 2023 freeCodeCamp course that installs Postgres, walks the schema, then works through queries, functions and administration with pgAdmin and psql. Postgres is the default serious database and this is a clean on-ramp.

title: Learn PostgreSQL Tutorial - Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: The longer 2019 course — four hours and twenty minutes — with more time on joins, indexing and administration than the 2023 version. Still accurate because Postgres' core semantics have not changed.

title: MongoDB Zero to Hero in 83 Minutes | Complete course with Realtime Projects
editorNote: Eighty-three minutes, published 2026, covering documents, queries, the aggregation pipeline and wiring Mongo into a small application with a real project. Current enough to reflect MongoDB 8-era drivers.

title: Learn MongoDB in 1 hour 🍃
editorNote: A one-hour tour of Mongo's shell and mental model, formatted for skimming. Enough to evaluate whether a document store fits your data.

title: Redis Crash Course
editorNote: Twenty-eight minutes that cover what Redis is good for, the core data types and the caching patterns that actually show up in production — with clear distinctions about when not to use it.

title: SQL for Data Analytics – Intermediate Course + Project
editorNote: A 2025 intermediate course that ends in a portfolio project — load a real dataset, answer questions with SQL, present the result. The best 'prove you can use SQL' artefact in the database category.

title: Learn HTML & CSS – Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Five hours that build real pages — semantic HTML first, then CSS layout with flexbox and grid — rather than touring tags and properties. Each section ends by styling a working page, which is what makes the knowledge stick.

title: Learn HTML – Full Tutorial for Beginners
editorNote: Four hours dedicated to HTML alone: document structure, text, links, images, tables, forms and validation. Slower and more thorough than the combined HTML/CSS courses, which matters because semantics cause most accessibility bugs later.

title: CSS Tutorial – Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Eleven hours that go from selectors to responsive design, transitions and modern layout without skipping the box model. The most complete CSS reference course verified, and the one to return to when a layout refuses to behave.

title: Web Development with HTML & CSS – Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Almost twenty hours spent building a complete website from a design, in real time. It is the closest thing to pair-programming with an instructor, and the output is portfolio-ready.

title: HTML Tutorial for Beginners: HTML Crash Course
editorNote: Seventy minutes to a first working page by an instructor who has taught this material for a decade. Use it to get moving, then take the long HTML course for semantics.

title: Tailwind CSS v4 for Beginners | Full Course 2026
editorNote: A 2026 course on Tailwind v4 — the current major version, including the new CSS-first configuration — taught by building layouts rather than listing classes. Tailwind changed enough in v4 that older courses teach configuration that no longer exists.

title: Learn Tailwind CSS – Course for Beginners
editorNote: Four hours and a small project, published 2023 — still useful for its component-building patterns, but written for Tailwind v3, so check the v4 course first for configuration.

title: Learn Accessibility - Full a11y Tutorial
editorNote: Ninety minutes covering semantic HTML as the first accessibility tool, then ARIA, keyboard navigation, colour contrast and testing with a screen reader. Frames accessibility as correct markup rather than an add-on checklist.

title: The Only Accessibility Video You Will Ever Need
editorNote: Thirty-eight minutes of the highest-signal accessibility advice — focus management, labels, contrast — condensed for developers who need the essentials before shipping.

title: JavaScript Full Course for free 🌐
editorNote: Twelve hours from variables to async/await with small projects after every section, published 2024. The most complete free JavaScript course verified that is embeddable — the popular SuperSimpleDev alternative disables embedding, so this is the practical best pick.

title: JavaScript Course for Beginners
editorNote: A 2024 freeCodeCamp course — three and a half hours — with a slower pace and more explanation than most: every concept gets a demonstration plus a small build. Best first JavaScript course for learners who found the 12-hour courses intimidating.

title: JavaScript Course for Beginners – Your First Step to Web Development
editorNote: Under an hour of carefully sequenced essentials. The fastest way for an experienced programmer to pick up JavaScript syntax and quirks.

title: TypeScript Full Course - From Beginner to Advanced
editorNote: A 2024 course that moves from primitives to generics, narrowing and typed React, then builds a project with the type system doing real work. Better than syntax-tour courses for developers who already know JavaScript.

title: Learn TypeScript - Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Two hours, published 2024, starting from 'what problem does TypeScript solve' — ideal for learners who want types without a heavy generics detour on day one.

title: TypeScript Tutorial for Beginners
editorNote: One hour of TypeScript for an experienced developer: annotations, interfaces, unions, generics, classes, then a typed project skeleton.

title: JavaScript Tutorials for Beginners
editorNote: 47 short episodes covering one JavaScript idea each, useful as a lookup library when a specific concept needs a second explanation. Not a substitute for a linear course.

title: Learn JavaScript - Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: The classic 2018 freeCodeCamp JavaScript course — still the most-watched free JS course on YouTube and still accurate on the language, though it predates modern tooling entirely.

title: React JS 19 Full Course 2025 | Build an App and Master React in 2 Hours
editorNote: React 19 taught entirely through building an app — components, state, effects, props, routing — in two hours. It is the narrowest gap between starting and shipping something real, and it is version-current.

title: React Full Course for free ⚛️
editorNote: Nearly five hours in an ordered curriculum — components, props, state, effects, forms, context, router — with a project after each block. The most systematic free React course in the verified set.

title: All React Hooks Explained - React Hooks Tutorial 2025
editorNote: Every important hook explained and demonstrated in ninety minutes, including the rules of hooks and custom hooks. The best single revision resource before a React interview or a refactor.

title: React Tutorial for Beginners
editorNote: Eighty minutes from empty folder to a working React app with components, state, effects and API calls, edited so that nothing non-essential survives. It is the shortest path we found to a first running app for someone who already knows JavaScript, and it is deliberately scoped — routing, context and testing are left to the full courses.

title: Next.js 16 Full Course | Build and Deploy a Production-Ready Full Stack App
editorNote: A four-hour build of a production-style application on Next.js 16 — App Router, server components, data fetching, auth, deployment. Published late 2025, it teaches the version that is actually current.

title: Next.js Tutorial 2026 (UPDATED) - Full Course - Start Your Next.js Journey Here
editorNote: An updated 2026 Next.js tutorial built around explaining the mental model of the App Router before writing code. The clearest short introduction to how Next.js differs from plain React.

title: Next.js Full Tutorial - Beginner to Advanced
editorNote: Seven hours that go beyond the happy path — caching layers, revalidation, parallel routes, middleware, data patterns. The resource to use once a Next.js project gets past the tutorial stage.

title: Full Modern React Tutorial
editorNote: 32 short episodes that build one React application incrementally — the original modern React tutorial series, still a clean way to see a project grow step by step.

title: MERN Stack Tutorial for Beginners with Deployment – 2025
editorNote: A 2025 end-to-end MERN build with deployment — the whole loop of a modern web application in one sitting. Best used after React and Node basics so the value is in integration and deployment rather than syntax.

title: Intro to Backend Web Development – Node.js & Express Tutorial for Beginners
editorNote: A 2025 freeCodeCamp introduction to backend development with Node and Express: HTTP, routing, middleware, REST design, error handling. Current, and it teaches the concepts rather than only the framework API.

title: Backend Complete Course | NodeJS, ExpressJS, JWT, PostgreSQL, Prisma...
editorNote: A 2025 backend course that assembles the real stack — Express, JWT authentication, PostgreSQL, Prisma — into a working service. Published recently enough that the library versions are the ones you will actually install.

title: JWT Authentication Tutorial - Node.js
editorNote: A thirty-minute implementation of JWT authentication in Node, including refresh tokens and the security trade-offs of each storage choice. Short, correct and directly reusable.

title: What Is JWT and Why Should You Use JWT
editorNote: Fifteen minutes that explain what a JWT actually contains, how the signature proves the payload has not been tampered with, and when a plain session cookie is the better design. The right first watch before implementing token auth, and a useful correction for the 'JWT everywhere' habit.

title: Python API Development - Comprehensive Course for Beginners
editorNote: Nineteen hours that build a production-shaped API — database models, migrations, automated testing, CI and container deployment — not just endpoints. The most complete Python API engineering course verified.

title: FastAPI Crash Course - Modern Python API Development
editorNote: A one-hour 2026 FastAPI crash course, updated for current Pydantic and FastAPI versions. The quickest way to see modern Python API development end to end.

title: React Node.js Real Estate App Full Tutorial | MERN Stack App & Real-time Chat
editorNote: Five hours building a real-estate application with authentication, image uploads, chat and a database — the closest free equivalent to a bootcamp capstone project.

title: Docker Tutorial for Beginners [FULL COURSE in 3 Hours]
editorNote: Three hours that explain images, containers, volumes, networking and Compose with animated diagrams and then demonstrate each one. The mental model first approach is why this remains the reference Docker introduction.

title: Learn Docker – Full DevOps Course for Deploying Containerized Apps
editorNote: Seven and a half hours, published late 2025, that carry an application from Dockerfile to registry to deployment with multi-stage builds and Compose. The modern follow-on to the introductory course.

title: Ultimate Docker Compose Tutorial
editorNote: A focused hour on Compose: services, networks, volumes, environment handling and the file structure that keeps multi-container projects sane.

title: Learn Kubernetes in 6 Hours – Full Course with Real-World Project
editorNote: A six-hour 2025 course that deploys a real application to Kubernetes across local clusters and a managed cloud cluster: pods, deployments, services, ingress, configuration and autoscaling, in the order you meet them in production.

title: Kubernetes Tutorial for Beginners [FULL COURSE in 4 Hours]
editorNote: Three and a half hours built on clear diagrams of the control plane and worker nodes, then hands-on with kubectl. The gentle introduction that makes the longer courses feel obvious.

title: Complete Kubernetes Course - From BEGINNER to PRO
editorNote: Beyond the beginner path: stateful workloads, network policies, RBAC, operators and cluster upgrades, with a real application carried through. For engineers who already deploy to Kubernetes and keep meeting the same walls.

title: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner Certification Course 2026 (CLF-C02) - Pass the Exam!
editorNote: A thirteen-and-a-half-hour 2026 course aligned to the current CLF-C02 exam, covering IAM, compute, storage, networking, billing and architecture. Even if you skip the exam, it is the most systematic tour of what cloud providers actually offer.

title: Terraform Course - Automate your AWS cloud infrastructure
editorNote: Two and a half hours provisioning real AWS infrastructure with Terraform — providers, variables, state, modules — ending with a reproducible environment. The best free introduction to treating infrastructure as code.

title: Complete GitHub Actions Course - From BEGINNER to PRO
editorNote: A complete GitHub Actions course — workflow syntax, caching, matrix builds, containers, security and deployment pipelines — with real repositories to follow. Published 2025, so it matches current runner images and actions.

title: System Design Course – APIs, Databases, Caching, CDNs, Load Balancing & Production Infra
editorNote: A 2025 freeCodeCamp system design course covering APIs, database choices, caching, CDNs, load balancing and observability with diagrams and worked examples. The most current end-to-end treatment verified.

title: System Design Concepts Course and Interview Prep
editorNote: Fifty minutes of interview framing — how to structure an answer, what interviewers probe, and the handful of concepts that decide most outcomes.

title: System Design Interview: A Step-By-Step Guide
editorNote: A ten-minute illustrated pass over the whole system design landscape — exactly the orientation a learner needs before a two-hour course.

title: JavaScript Clean Code Course – Fix Code Smells & Refactor
editorNote: A 2025 course that takes real messy JavaScript and refactors it in front of you, naming the smell before the fix. Concrete refactoring beats abstract principles, and this is the best example of that format in the verified set.

title: Introduction To Testing In JavaScript With Jest
editorNote: Fourteen minutes that establish what a unit test is, how to write one with Jest and when mocking is a smell — enough to start putting tests in your own project today.

title: Testing In React Tutorial - Jest and React Testing Library
editorNote: Twenty-one minutes testing React components the way users interact with them — queries by role and text rather than by implementation detail — which is the habit that keeps tests from breaking on every refactor.

title: Software Testing Explained in 100 Seconds
editorNote: Two minutes that sort unit, integration and end-to-end testing into the right order of investment. Useful as the first hit of context before writing any tests.

title: My 10 “Clean” Code Principles (Start These Now)
editorNote: Fifteen minutes of unusually honest engineering advice — version small, write tests for the scary parts, delete dead code — framed as habits rather than rules.

title: Learn Data Science Tutorial - Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Six hours that answer 'what does a data scientist actually do' — collecting data, cleaning it, exploring, modelling, communicating — with Python throughout. The right orientation before specialising in statistics or machine learning.

title: Pandas & Python for Data Analysis by Example – Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Five hours of pure pandas by example: loading, cleaning, filtering, grouping, joining, reshaping and plotting real datasets in notebooks. The most complete free pandas course verified and the core skill behind every data-science path.

title: Complete Python Pandas Data Science Tutorial! (2025 Updated Edition)
editorNote: Keith Galli's updated pandas tutorial — one and a half hours, refreshed in 2024/2025, with a cleaner narrative than the long courses and modern pandas idioms.

title: Learn Pandas in 30 Minutes - Python Pandas Tutorial
editorNote: Thirty-one minutes, published 2025, covering the DataFrame operations used in 90% of day-to-day analysis. Ideal before starting a real dataset.

title: Learn Pandas in Under 3 Hours | Filtering, Joins, Indexing, Data Cleaning, Visualizations
editorNote: A 2024 analyst-oriented pandas course — filtering, joins, indexing, cleaning — structured the way analytics work is actually assigned.

title: 1. Introduction to Statistics
editorNote: MIT's opening statistics lecture: what statistics is for, sampling, variability and descriptive measures, taught with the rigour you would expect and no hand-waving. The strongest foundation available free if you intend to trust your models.

title: Complete Statistics For Data Science In 6 hours By Krish Naik
editorNote: Six hours covering descriptive statistics, distributions, sampling, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing with worked examples — the applied statistics course that most data-science learners actually need.

title: Machine Learning Course for Beginners
editorNote: Ten hours of machine-learning fundamentals with Python — regression, classification, clustering, model evaluation — built around scikit-learn and real datasets. Broad enough to be a curriculum and practical enough to produce working models.

title: Python Machine Learning Tutorial (Data Science)
editorNote: Fifty minutes that take you from a CSV to a trained, evaluated model with Jupyter and scikit-learn. The quickest honest answer to 'what does training a model feel like'.

title: AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Generative AI Explained
editorNote: Ten minutes that clearly separate AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI — including what each is not. Worth watching before any AI roadmap so the vocabulary stops blurring.

title: MLOps Course – Build Machine Learning Production Grade Projects
editorNote: Three hours that take a model past the notebook: experiment tracking with MLflow, packaging with Docker, deployment and monitoring. The transition every ML learner needs and most courses skip.

title: Machine Learning
editorNote: freeCodeCamp's machine-learning collection — including the 'Machine Learning for Everybody' course — gathered in one place. Useful as a curated shelf once you finish a first course and want breadth.

title: But what is a neural network? | Deep learning chapter 1
editorNote: The best visual explanation of what a neural network is doing — layers, weights, activations — created by 3Blue1Brown and viewed over 24 million times. Nothing else establishes the geometric intuition this quickly, and the whole playlist is only 3.5 hours.

title: Transformers, the tech behind LLMs | Deep Learning Chapter 5
editorNote: Twenty-seven minutes that make attention and the transformer block visually obvious — the architecture behind every modern LLM. Watch this before any LLM engineering work and the engineering literature becomes readable.

title: Attention in transformers, step-by-step | Deep Learning Chapter 6
editorNote: The step-by-step companion to the transformer chapter: queries, keys, values, masking and multi-head attention worked through with equations and animation. The clearest treatment of the mechanism itself.

title: How might LLMs store facts | Deep Learning Chapter 7
editorNote: Explores how facts might be stored in a model's MLP layers — the most concrete public treatment of what is happening inside an LLM beyond the attention mechanism.

title: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out.
editorNote: Andrej Karpathy builds a working GPT in PyTorch line by line, explaining every design decision. Two hours that convert transformer theory into code you have personally written — still the single highest-value deep-learning video for engineers.

title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
editorNote: Ten videos building neural networks from scratch — backpropagation with micrograd, language models with makemore, then the GPT build. Around nineteen hours total and the most rigorous free path from intuition to implementation.

title: PyTorch for Deep Learning & Machine Learning – Full Course
editorNote: Twenty-five hours of PyTorch with a project-driven structure — tensors, autograd, training loops, datasets, transfer learning, then three real projects including computer vision. Effectively a full deep-learning curriculum in one video.

title: Deep Learning With PyTorch - Full Course
editorNote: A four-and-a-half-hour PyTorch course with a clean linear progression — tensors, autograd, training, CNNs, RNNs — useful when the 25-hour course feels like too much to schedule.

title: Learn PyTorch for deep learning in a day. Literally.
editorNote: The 'Learn PyTorch for deep learning in a day' course — nearly 26 hours, with notebooks, exercises and extra-curricular problems. A structured alternative to the freeCodeCamp course with a strong emphasis on doing rather than watching.

title: Stanford CS230 | Autumn 2025 | Lecture 1: Introduction to Deep Learning
editorNote: Stanford CS230's current (autumn 2025) opening lecture: what deep learning is, how the course builds, and the practical advice on data, splits and metrics that the lectures emphasise. The academic anchor for a self-taught deep-learning path.

title: Deep Learning Crash Course for Beginners
editorNote: Eighty-six minutes that cover the main architecture families — dense, convolutional, recurrent — with code, so you see what each is for before committing to a framework course.

title: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
editorNote: Three and a half hours covering the entire life of a modern LLM — pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, tokenisation, hallucinations and tool use — with demos of each stage. Published February 2025, it is the most current deep overview from someone who has trained these models.

title: [1hr Talk] Intro to Large Language Models
editorNote: The one-hour talk that defined the genre: what an LLM is, how it is trained, what it can and cannot do, and how to think about security and tool use. Non-technical enough for product and business readers while staying accurate.

title: How I use LLMs
editorNote: A two-hour demonstration of using LLM tools well in real work — context management, model choice, tool integration, where they fail. The best complement to any prompt-engineering course because it shows judgement rather than templates.

title: AI Engineer Roadmap – How to Learn AI in 2025
editorNote: Fifty-five minutes mapping the AI engineer role — what to learn, in what order, and which parts of traditional ML matter for application work. Useful orientation before committing to a multi-month path.

title: AI Foundations for Absolute Beginners
editorNote: A 2026 freeCodeCamp course for absolute beginners — what AI systems are, how they are trained, and how to use a pretrained model in code without a maths detour first.

title: Production-Grade AI Project Tutorial – Build & Deploy
editorNote: A 2025 freeCodeCamp build that takes an AI feature all the way to a deployed service — model calls, API layer, container, deployment. The clearest demonstration of the difference between a notebook demo and a production AI application.

title: Train Your Own LLM – Tutorial
editorNote: A 2025 tutorial that trains a small language model on your own data — tokeniser, dataset preparation, training loop, evaluation. Demystifies 'training a model' without requiring a cluster.

title: What is a Vector Database? Powering Semantic Search & AI Applications
editorNote: Ten minutes that explain what a vector database does, how similarity search works and when a library like FAISS is enough instead. The right orientation before choosing infrastructure.

title: Large Language Models explained briefly
editorNote: Eight minutes of the clearest possible explanation of what an LLM is and how it produces text. Ideal first watch in the generative AI category, and short enough to send to a non-technical teammate.

title: GenAI Essentials – Full Course for Beginners
editorNote: Twenty-three hours published January 2025 covering the whole generative AI stack — model landscape, prompting, embeddings, RAG, agents, evaluation — as one coherent curriculum. The best single video to understand the entire field's vocabulary in context.

title: Generative AI for Developers – Comprehensive Course
editorNote: Twenty-one hours aimed squarely at developers: APIs, embeddings, vector stores, RAG and agents with code from the first hour. More engineering-dense than the essentials course.

title: Generative AI Full Course – Gemini Pro, OpenAI, Llama, Langchain, Pinecone, Vector Databases & More
editorNote: Thirty hours of project-based generative AI — Gemini, OpenAI, Llama, LangChain, Pinecone, vector databases — with many small applications built. Use it as a project catalogue: pick the ones that match your roadmap rather than watching linearly.

title: Full AI Prompting Course with Andrew Ng
editorNote: DeepLearning.AI's 2026 prompting course with Andrew Ng — updated to include agents, reasoning models and evaluation alongside classic principles. The official-quality option in a field crowded with prompt 'hacks'.

title: Prompt Engineering Full Course
editorNote: Thirty-eight minutes, published 2026, showing the prompting patterns that survive contact with real models — few-shot, decomposition, output structure, critique loops — with live examples.

title: Vector Embeddings Tutorial – Code Your Own AI Assistant with GPT-4 API + LangChain + NLP
editorNote: Thirty-six minutes that build a working question-answering assistant on embeddings, including the chunking and similarity decisions that make or break results. Concrete enough to reuse the architecture immediately.

title: Getting Started with Pinecone
editorNote: Pinecone's own 2025 getting-started walkthrough — index creation, upserts, queries — the vendor-official path to a working vector database. Use it after the conceptual videos to have something running.

title: RAG Crash Course for Beginners
editorNote: Fifty-nine minutes published September 2025 that walk the full RAG loop — ingest, chunk, embed, retrieve, generate, evaluate — with the failure modes named as they appear. The most current short RAG course verified.

title: Learn RAG From Scratch – Python AI Tutorial from a LangChain Engineer
editorNote: Two and a half hours from a LangChain engineer that go well past naive RAG — query rewriting, routing, multi-index retrieval, re-ranking — with runnable notebooks. The technical depth layer after a first RAG course.

title: Complete RAG Playlist
editorNote: Eight videos covering RAG end to end with LangChain and vector stores — a compact playlist for learners who prefer many short sessions to one long video.

title: LLM Fine-Tuning Course – From Supervised FT to RLHF, LoRA, and Multimodal
editorNote: Twelve hours published in 2026 covering the full adaptation spectrum — supervised fine-tuning, LoRA/QLoRA, RLHF and DPO, up to multimodal models. The most complete and most current fine-tuning resource verified.

title: How to Systematically Setup LLM Evals (Metrics, Unit Tests, LLM-as-a-Judge)
editorNote: Fifty-five minutes that treat evaluation as engineering: define metrics, write unit tests for prompts, use LLM-as-judge carefully, and track regressions. The most actionable evaluation resource for people shipping LLM features.

title: What is Multimodal AI? How LLMs Process Text, Images, and More
editorNote: A 2026 explainer on how models process text, images and audio together, including what multimodal actually enables in products. Fast, accurate orientation for the multimodal skill.

title: Agentic AI – Complete Course for Beginners
editorNote: Twenty-four hours published July 2026 — the most current and most complete agentic AI course verified: agent loops, tool calling, memory, planning, multi-agent patterns and production concerns, each with implementations. This is the spine of the agentic roadmap.

title: Full Course (Lessons 1-10) AI Agents for Beginners
editorNote: Microsoft's 'AI Agents for Beginners' lessons 1–10 in a single hour: what an agent is, tool use, planning, memory, evaluation — vendor-official teaching material with small code samples. The best structured first contact with agents.

title: OpenAI Function Calling - Full Beginner Tutorial
editorNote: Twenty-eight minutes that implement function calling properly: schema design, argument validation, error handling and the loop back into the model. The primitive underneath every agent framework, taught directly.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Explained for Beginners: AI Flight Booking Demo!
editorNote: Twenty-four minutes that explain MCP — servers, clients, resources, tools, prompts — and then demonstrate it with a working flight-booking example. The demo is what makes the protocol click.

title: Model Context Protocol Clearly Explained | MCP Beyond the Hype
editorNote: Fifteen minutes of unusually clear explanation of why MCP exists, what problem it solves and how it differs from simply writing function calls.

title: Intro to MCP Servers – Model Context Protocol with Python Course
editorNote: Seventy-three minutes of hands-on MCP server construction in Python — tools, resources, prompts, transport, and connecting the server to a client. Published October 2025, so it matches the current protocol revision.

title: Build Anything With a CUSTOM MCP Server - Python Tutorial
editorNote: A focused 26-minute build of a custom MCP server that connects a model to a real external service — the shortest path from understanding MCP to having your own server running.

title: LangGraph Complete Course for Beginners – Complex AI Agents with Python
editorNote: Three hours building agents as explicit graphs — state, nodes, edges, conditional routing, persistence. LangGraph forces the control flow to be visible, which is exactly the skill that separates reliable agents from prompt spaghetti.

title: Agentic AI Crash Course using LangChain | LangChain Crash Course
editorNote: A 2026 LangChain crash course — two and a half hours — covering chains, tools, agents and memory with current library versions. Useful as the framework tour, best taken after understanding the underlying tool-calling loop.

title: The Four Types of Memory Every AI Agent Needs
editorNote: Eleven minutes that separate the memory types agents actually need — short-term context, long-term facts, episodic history, procedural knowledge — and how each is implemented. Prevents the common mistake of treating 'memory' as one feature.

title: Guide to Agentic AI – Build a Python Coding Agent with Gemini
editorNote: Two hours building a coding agent with the Gemini API — file editing tools, sandboxing, iteration loops — the architecture behind tools like code assistants. A strong project after the MCP and tool-calling resources.

title: Build Hour: Agents SDK
editorNote: OpenAI's own May 2026 build hour on the Agents SDK — the vendor-official walkthrough of agents, handoffs, guardrails and tracing. Included as the official reference point for the category.

title: OpenAI Assistants API – Course for Beginners
editorNote: Three and a half hours on hosted assistant APIs — tools, file search, code interpreter and threads — a different architecture from building your own loop. Still the most thorough free treatment of managed agent platforms.

title: AI Safety – Full Course by Safe.AI Founder on Machine Learning & Ethics (Center for AI Safety)
editorNote: Eight and a half hours from a Safe.AI founder covering alignment, robustness, bias, privacy and governance with practical exercises. The most substantive free treatment of AI safety rather than a checklist of principles.

title: The Complete AI Security Course In 8 Hours-AI Guardrails, LLM Evals & Memory And AgentOps
editorNote: An eight-hour 2026 course on securing AI systems — prompt injection, guardrails, evaluation and memory risks — the operational counterpart to AI safety theory, aimed at people deploying agents.

title: Harvard CS50’s Intro to Cybersecurity – Full University Course
editorNote: Harvard's CS50 Cybersecurity as one 7-hour university course: authentication, access control, cryptography, web security, privacy — with problem sets that are actually challenging. Published October 2025 and the best-structured free security foundation.

title: Computer Networking Fundamentals Course
editorNote: Twelve hours published February 2026 — the most complete and current networking course verified: OSI and TCP/IP models, Ethernet, IP addressing, routing, DNS, HTTP, TLS, plus troubleshooting with real tools.

title: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Full Certification Course
editorNote: A 2025 full Network+ (N10-009) course taught with clear animations — the fastest way to cover certification-grade networking breadth, and a good second voice on any topic that did not land the first time.

title: Hands-On Cybersecurity and Ethical Hacking – Full Course
editorNote: Three and a half hours published February 2026 doing hands-on offensive work in legal labs — reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation and reporting. Current tooling, and it keeps the legal and ethical boundary explicit throughout.

title: Ethical Hacking in 12 Hours - Full Course - Learn to Hack!
editorNote: Twelve hours of practical ethical-hacking instruction with a lab-heavy structure, covering reconnaissance through exploitation and post-exploitation. The classic long course in this category.

title: Wireshark Tutorial for Beginners | Network Scanning Made Easy
editorNote: Twenty minutes with Wireshark on real traffic: capture, filters, following streams, and spotting scanning activity. The practical packet-analysis skill that makes networking concrete.

title: OWASP API Security Top 10 Course – Secure Your Web Apps
editorNote: Eighty-seven minutes walking the OWASP API Security Top 10 with exploitable examples and fixes for each category. APIs are where modern breaches happen and this is the most practical free treatment verified.

title: Introduction to Web Security | Web Security Crash Course
editorNote: Forty-six minutes that demonstrate the classic web vulnerabilities — XSS, CSRF, SQL injection, session issues — in a browser, so the abstract categories become visible attacks.

title: Security Operations (SOC) 101 Course - 10+ Hours of Content!
editorNote: A 10+ hour SOC analyst course published 2025: SIEM work, alert triage, detection engineering, threat intelligence and reporting, with lab-style walkthroughs. The most complete blue-team resource verified.

title: Cybersecurity IDR: Incident Detection & Response | Google Cybersecurity Certificate
editorNote: Google's own incident-detection-and-response module from the Cybersecurity Certificate: the NIST-aligned lifecycle, detection sources, escalation and post-incident review. Vendor-official, free and clearly presented.

title: Google Cybersecurity Certificate
editorNote: The Google Cybersecurity Certificate lectures as a playlist — 39 videos covering foundations, networks, Linux, SQL, detection and response. A structured career path rather than a single topic.

title: AWS Security Explained: Shared Responsibility Model, Compliance and IAM | AWS Tutorial | KodeKloud
editorNote: Thirty minutes on the shared responsibility model, IAM, and the misconfigurations that cause most cloud breaches. The clearest short treatment of what security looks like in the cloud.

title: 5 Steps to Secure Linux (protect from hackers)
editorNote: Twenty-three minutes of the five changes that remove most easy Linux compromise paths — SSH key-only auth, firewall rules, updates, users, sudo. High impact per minute, and demonstrated on a live server.

title: Hacker unlocks Cryptography secrets (hashing, encryption and more)
editorNote: A ninety-minute conversation-and-demo on what cryptography actually does — hashing, symmetric and asymmetric encryption, key exchange, where implementations break. Accurate, practical and free of hand-waving.

title: Git and GitHub Tutorial for Beginners [11 Hours]
editorNote: Eleven hours that go past 'git init, git commit' into the parts beginners actually get stuck on: branching strategies, merge vs rebase, resolving conflicts, cherry-pick, tagged releases and the full GitHub pull-request workflow. Use it when the crash courses run out, or as a reference you watch one chapter at a time when a real repository misbehaves.

title: System Design Interview Prep for Beginners (Full Course)
editorNote: A 2026 refresh of the system design basics from KodeKloud: requirements, load balancers, caching, database choices and the trade-offs behind each, aimed at people who have never designed a service. It is the gentlest on-ramp in this category and it is genuinely current, so a beginner is not learning architecture from a decade-old diagram.

title: How to Prepare for System Design Interviews w/ Meta Staff Engineer
editorNote: An 18-minute walkthrough by a Meta staff engineer of how system design interviews are actually evaluated: how to scope requirements, talk through trade-offs and drive the conversation instead of silently drawing boxes. Small commitment, and it reframes the interview as communication.

title: Machine Learning for Everybody – Full Course
editorNote: Kylie Ying teaches classical machine learning the way it is actually practised: load a dataset, split it, fit a scikit-learn model, read the metrics, then fix what went wrong. Regression, classification, clustering and neural-network basics all appear with runnable notebooks, and the failure cases (overfitting, leakage, bad metrics) get as much time as the successes.

title: All Machine Learning algorithms explained in 17 min
editorNote: Sixteen animated minutes that put every common algorithm on one map — supervised, unsupervised, ensembles, boosting — so the names stop being noise. Best used before or alongside a full course, not instead of one.

title: Statistics - A Full Lecture to learn Data Science (2025 Version)
editorNote: A five-hour statistics lecture that stays on the concepts that show up in real analysis work — descriptive statistics, distributions, sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing — with the reasoning shown rather than formula-dumped. Statistics is the part of data science that ages slowest and gets skipped fastest.

title: Linux System Administration Full Course
editorNote: Six hours on running a Linux machine rather than using one: users and groups, file permissions, package and service management, storage, logs and the basic networking commands an operator is expected to know. Complements the command-line courses by showing the system behind the shell.

title: Google Cloud Associate Cloud Engineer Course - Pass the Exam!
editorNote: Twenty hours of guided Google Cloud labs covering compute, storage, networking, IAM, containers and monitoring — the multi-cloud counterweight to the AWS course in this category. The console walkthroughs and quiz-style pacing make it the most practical free route into a second cloud.

title: Ollama Course – Build AI Apps Locally
editorNote: Builds working apps against locally hosted models with Ollama — chat with your documents, a coding assistant, vision and an image-generation pipeline — with no API keys and no per-token cost. Essential counterweight to the cloud-API tutorials: it teaches the same application patterns while making model hosting, quantisation and privacy trade-offs visible.

title: Git and GitHub for Beginners - Crash Course
editorNote: Seventy minutes that get a beginner from 'what is version control' to pushing branches and opening a pull request on a real GitHub repository, at a pace you can follow live. Useful as the fastest complete first pass when a multi-hour course is more commitment than the moment allows.
